title: Accessible charts with a data table fallback
when: Any page that shows a chart, or a review of an existing chart for accessibility.
prompt:
Goal: Every chart has a message title, a text summary, a real data table and keyboard access, and never relies on color alone.
Steps:
1. Headline the takeaway ("Returns fell after the new size guide"), not just the metric.
2. svg gets role="img" and aria-labelledby pointing at the heading and a summary paragraph; internals are aria-hidden.
3. Provide a <table> with <caption>, th scope="col" headers and th scope="row" labels, in <details><summary>Show data</summary>.
4. Encode series beyond color: direct labels, dash patterns or marker shapes; marks reach 3 to 1 contrast.
5. Interactive points are reachable by Tab or arrows and show the same readout on focus as on hover.
6. Respect prefers-reduced-motion for drawing animations; text stays at least 12 px when scaled down.
Quality bar:
- Screen reader users get the message and the numbers.
- Grayscale printing keeps series apart.
- Table and chart come from the same data.
Pitfalls:
- A title that just says "Chart".
- Values only in hover tooltips.
- A separately typed table that drifts from the chart.
Verify:
- [ ] svg has role img and a name.
- [ ] Table has caption and th headers.
- [ ] Series distinguishable without color.
- [ ] Visible focus on interactive points.
Output: Chart markup with heading, summary and table, plus chart.css for focus and patterns.

examples.input: make my dashboard charts usable with a screen reader
examples.output: takeaway headings, aria-labelledby summaries, Show data tables with captions, dashed second series
